extracted.intended_audience: student journalists and practicing news reporters
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of exemplar newspaper pieces illustrating various types of short news/feature reporting (parades, holiday charity pieces, theatre reviews, society banquets, school/charity entertainments, satire). Useful as models for writing event/features copy and for understanding what elements each type typically includes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorial Day procession / veterans parade
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on a public procession: describe turnout, weather, crowd enthusiasm, veteran participants (age, wounds, uniforms), flags and pageantry, the order of march, notable officers and dignitaries, and include short quotations from participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid scene-setting (weather, flags, crowd size — e.g., “Probably more than 50,000 people”), physical detail of marchers (old age, canes, uniforms, medals), names and titles of commanders and marshals, list organizations in the procession, and include a humanizing quote (example: George Sebech: “I am 98 years old, but I’ll be marching here ten years from now…”). Emphasize sensory detail and chronology (who led, who followed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Christmas charity / civic-organizations feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of community-wide charitable Christmas efforts: describe organizational coordination, modes of distribution (baskets, dinners), institutional participation, and the scale of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the organizational structure (e.g., Associated Charities, Salvation Army, churches), list concrete actions (turkey dinners, baskets, coal/clothing gifts), cite numbers where available (e.g., ‘‘2,000 names on the list’’ or quantities of baskets), name organizers and headquarters, and show how traditions were adapted (motor trucks replacing sleighs). Provide examples of cooperative efforts and logistical details to convey scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children’s hospital human-interest feature
rubrics_metrics.description: A human-interest vignette centered on sick or convalescing children during holiday events, emphasizing emotion, dialogue, and the spectacle of the celebration in a medical setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on intimate, often dialogue-driven moments (snippets of child conversation), physical conditions described sensitively (spinal trouble, strapped to a board), sensory imagery (tree touching the ceiling, toys, songs), named caregivers (nurses, teachers) and performers, and juxtapose illness with joy. Include program details (music, who performed) and note ongoing visits/performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pantomime / outdoor theatrical review
rubrics_metrics.description: Short review/preview of a public theatrical performance: describe setting, audience conditions, timing, cast of characters, plot highlights, and notable stage effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with scene-setting (late hour, lighting, weather), mention attendance and crowd behavior, list principal characters and roles (e.g., ‘The Seven Gifts’ cast), summarize key scenes and dramatic/highlight moments (gift sequence, Pierrot/Moon Lady episode), note production choices (placards explaining action, concealed band, stage lighting), and evaluate accessibility (many left due to crowding). Use narrative description rather than academic critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humorous/satirical short column (society joke obit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lightly satirical, humorous short item imitating obituary/society copy to lampoon a topical subject (e.g., 'Last Day for Straw Hats').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt mock-formal obituary or society tone, use puns and wordplay, invent playful biographical details, include faux mournful ceremony descriptions, and end with a witty epitaph. Brevity and comic voice are central; avoid negative personal attacks and keep satire topical and recognizable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banquet / society speech report
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of a formal banquet or society dinner focusing on principal speakers, themes of speeches, atmosphere, musical interludes, and notable attendees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize key toasts and speakers’ main points (e.g., Carnegie on Scotland: religion, politics, education), quote memorable lines, note ceremonial trappings (flags, music, kilts), list prominent guests, and include color details (bagpipe bands, orchestra). Convey tone of the evening (humorous, solemn) and highlight any notable claims or anecdotes introduced by speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: School entertainment / community performance report
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on a school or community theatrical presentation, with emphasis on participants, costumes, emotional impact, and educational value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the production (title, characters), highlight participants’ conditions when relevant (e.g., crippled children), name school officials (principal) and note audience reaction (tears, applause). Detail costumes and staging, and emphasize the uplifting/therapeutic role of the performance for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children’s-hospital bedside visitation feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Short feature describing performers visiting patients at bedside, capturing personal interactions between performers/visitors and patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use close, dialogue-rich reporting, name the child and visitor, record tender exchanges and gestures (holding hands, requests to watch the show), include inscriptions/memorial details in the ward for human context, and note the schedule/structure of the larger performance that follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawn fete / charity pageant society report
rubrics_metrics.description: Society-style description of a charity garden fete or pageant: describe setting, costumes, participants, booths, and who staffed them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paint a visual picture of the garden setting, list character costumes and notable children, provide detailed costume descriptions (materials, colors, accessories), enumerate volunteers and booth-staff (names), and describe fundraising activities (sales of sweets, balloons). Focus on pageantry and charity purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious/jubilee service coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on a solemn religious service held to honor a dignitary or occasion, focusing on liturgy, ceremonial vestments, clergy positions, and the size and nature of the congregation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe ritual pomp (high mass, cassocks, stoles, acolytes), name officiating clergy and seating arrangement (e.g., Archbishop Farley at left of the chancel), characterize the congregation turnout and occasion (diamond jubilee for a monarch), and use formal, measured language appropriate to ceremonial reporting.
